references.text: Balak sends high-ranking officials together with Balaam, which is reflected in the sacrificial meal where Balak sends food to Balaam and 'the princes who were with him'.
Balak continues to offer cattle and small livestock together with Balaam at Bamoth-Baal, as part of the preparations to curse Israel.
Balak offers oxen and rams again; this pattern of sacrifice repeats throughout the story of Balak and Balaam.
Once more Balak offers cattle and small livestock, showing his repeated attempts to secure Balaam's curse through sacrifices.
Laban and Jacob ate together after making a covenant, illustrating the ancient custom of confirming agreements through meals.
The elders of Israel ate and drank in God's presence after the covenant was made, illustrating the connection between sacrifice, meal, and covenant.
